data.narrative: Completed Module 7 'Mid-Build Adaptation' learning about adapting plans when requirements change mid-execution, blast radius assessment to identify affected artifacts, preserving completed work rather than starting over, categorizing tickets as MUST/SHOULD/CUT for timeline management, and communicating impact honestly when scope grows.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted role-based access requirements from PM message: roles within organization (manager, employee, department head), permissions tied to roles, department structure, access control logic on booking endpoints
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-blast-radius.md Change 3 section documents role-based access requirements and their impact

dimension_scores.observation: Identified that role-based access escalates auth endpoints from NO IMPACT to MAJOR (JWT must carry role/department_id), seed database from NO IMPACT to MAJOR (need roles/departments seeded)
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-blast-radius.md shows escalation of POST /api/auth/login and Ticket 1 from NO IMPACT to MAJOR

dimension_scores.observation: Assessed that Option B (Minimal Bridge) is approaching Option A complexity with roles/departments/middleware but staying with Option B due to 6-day deadline. Cut payment processing from SHOULD SHIP to CUT to make room for role complexity
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-updated-plan.md decision re-evaluation: 'staying with Option B but acknowledging significantly increased risk'

dimension_scores.observation: Updated plan with clear categories (PRESERVED, MODIFIED, CUT, ADDED) and specific estimates for each ticket. Impact statement is specific and actionable with explicit acknowledgement of contradiction with original plan
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-updated-plan.md shows 4 modified tickets (8-12 hours), 9 added tickets (21-26 hours), total 29-38 hours over 6 days

dimension_scores.observation: Absorbed two requirement changes (company accounts, role-based access) within 15 minutes by layering changes on existing blast radius analysis, not rewriting from scratch. Updated plan 3 times without losing coherence
dimension_scores.evidence: module7_fix.md documents plan changed 3 times in module, built on adaptation not revert to scratch

dimension_scores.observation: Identified that role-based access requires JWT contract changes, middleware permission checks, and department filtering logic. Documented how these components integrate (JWT carries role, middleware enforces permissions, database stores role/department)
dimension_scores.evidence: module7_fix.md walkthrough: roles in data model, JWT carries role, middleware enforces permissions, employees rejected for delegation

strengths: Layered two requirement changes on existing plan without rewriting from scratch
Escalated impacts appropriately (auth from NO IMPACT to MAJOR, payment from SHOULD SHIP to CUT)
Acknowledged contradiction in impact statement to maintain PM credibility
Documented role-based access approach with specific integration details
data.recommendation: Use mid-build adaptation skills in real sprints where requirements change continuously - maintain current plan as living document, preserve completed work, communicate changes honestly

public_evidence.artifact: Updated plan with role-based access requirements
public_evidence.student_action: Adapted plan twice in 15 minutes for company accounts and role-based access requirements. Layered changes on existing blast radius analysis, escalated 4 tickets from NO IMPACT/MINOR to MAJOR, cut payment processing from SHOULD SHIP to CUT, added role/department tables and JWT contract. Total scope: 29-38 hours over 6 days.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Changes: roles table, departments table, user role/department_id columns, JWT payload with role/department_id, role-based middleware on booking endpoints, department filtering for department heads. Cuts: Payment Processing, Provider Self-Service, Real-Time Availability, Provider Dashboard, Search, Email Notifications.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to adapt plans when requirements change mid-execution without losing coherence, preserving completed work, assessing impact accurately, and communicating tradeoffs honestly to stakeholders

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Created blast radius table identifying impact of role-based access on database, API, frontend, contracts, tickets with NO IMPACT/MINOR/MAJOR/BLOCKED classifications
Updated plan 3 times in module by layering changes rather than rewriting from scratch, preserving original categorization structure

concepts_demonstrated.concept: Minimal bridge vs proper model tradeoff
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Recognized when role-based access pushed Option B to its limit but stayed with it due to deadline constraint, acknowledging increased risk

learning_style_signals: prefers concrete scenarios and structural layering
